sources.entry: Glowing Bear - A web frontend for WeeChat. (Demo) GPL-3.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Glowing Bear is a browser-based web client for the WeeChat IRC client that connects directly to a WeeChat relay over WebSockets.
summary.what_it_does: Glowing Bear is a web frontend for WeeChat, which does the IRC work on the server side while the client adds a modern interface. It connects from the browser straight to a WeeChat instance using the WeeChat relay plugin and WebSockets, with no intermediary backend service to install. It can embed images, videos and other content inline. It runs as a regular web page, as a Chrome app, or as a full-screen Android Chrome app, and the README also mentions Tauri-based standalone apps. The client is written in client-side JavaScript with some HTML and CSS. Developers can run a dev server with npm start or build static files with npm run build for hosting on a web server such as Caddy, nginx or Apache.
use_cases: access IRC from a phone or tablet
browse WeeChat sessions from any browser
self-host a web interface for WeeChat
view inline images and videos in IRC chat
run an IRC client as a home screen app
how_to_run: Open the Glowing Bear page in a browser and enter the WeeChat host and port
For development: clone the repository, run npm install, then npm start
To self-host: run npm run build and point a web server at the build/ folder
Run unit tests with npm test
notable: Connects directly from the browser to WeeChat over WebSockets, with no backend service
Installable as a Chrome app or Android home-screen app
Hosted version available on GitHub Pages, so self-hosting is optional
Uses the WeeChat relay plugin as its only backend
caveats: The quick-start relay setup is unencrypted and the README says not to use it over the internet without TLS
Requires WeeChat version 2.9 or later with a reachable relay port
Does not provide a way to reach machines behind a firewall through a server proxy, though a websocket proxy on a web server can be set up
